title: Chas Teaches Click — EN/ES/PT (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar Spanish Portuguese language learning dry wit deadpan 104bpm upright bass brushed snare absurdist comedy language lesson trilingual warm
lyrics:
[Verse 1 - English]
There are three main clicks in Xhosa and Zulu.
Chas has a sheet of paper and the confidence
of a man who has never attempted this before.
Joel got it on the second try. Chas took another sip of water.

[Verse 2 - Spanish, with English translations]
Hay tres chasquidos principales en Xhosa y Zulu. (There are three main clicks in Xhosa and Zulu.)
Chas tiene una hoja de papel y la confianza (Chas has a sheet of paper and the confidence)
de un hombre que nunca ha intentado esto antes. (of a man who has never attempted this before.)
Joel lo logró en el segundo intento. Chas tomó otro sorbo de agua. (Joel got it on the second try. Chas took another sip of water.)
Clic — no del todo eso. (Click — that's not quite it.)
Clic — acercándose a algo. (Click — getting closer to something.)
La sinceridad es la mayor parte de todo. (Sincerity is most of it.)

[Chorus - Portuguese, with English translations]
Clique (Click)
Isso não é bem isso (That's not quite it)
Clique (Click)
Chegando mais perto de algo (Getting closer to something)
Clique (Click)
A sala o encoraja (The room encourages him)
Clique (Click)
Joel conseguiu na segunda tentativa (Joel got it on the second try)
Clique (Click)
Chas tomou outro gole de água (Chas took another sip of water)
A sinceridade é a maior parte (Sincerity is most of it)

[Bridge - all three]
English: Sincerity, it turns out, is most of it.
Spanish: La sinceridad, resulta, es la mayor parte. (Sincerity, it turns out, is most of it.)
Portuguese: A sinceridade, descobre-se, é a maior parte. (Sincerity, it turns out, is most of it.)

[Outro - all three]
English: Chas Teaches Click — forty-five minutes — still going
Spanish: Chas enseña chasquido — cuarenta y cinco minutos — todavía va (Chas Teaches Click — forty-five minutes — still going)
Portuguese: Chas ensina clique — quarenta e cinco minutos — ainda vai (Chas Teaches Click — forty-five minutes — still going)
